text.p: The clean tanker market enjoyed a lively week, with medium range rates from the Middle East firming on a shortage of vessels, brokers said on Friday.
E.A. Gibson Shipwise said the long-range Middle East market was steady, with charterers still fixing for up to a month in advance.
But enquiries could fall off over the next two weeks due to Ramadan.
Rates to Japan remained at about W212.5 for 55,000 tonnes, brokers said.
They said rates in the Med and in inter-UKC had firmed markedly over the week, with cross-Med 30,000 tonne gas oil cargoes starting off at around W170-180 and reaching about W200 by Friday.

They also noted an armada of tankers carrying gasoline transatlantic, with between 825,000 and one million tonnes due to load in January to quench U.S. demand. Cargoes of 35,000 tonnes were fixed at W255 on Friday.
"At least 25 tankers have been fixed in the last six working days and there is more to come," one broker said.

Another broker said the transatlantic interest was boosting the UKC products market, with 20,000 tonne gas oil cargoes rising to W240 from W230 over the last couple of days. Although 25,000 tonne cargoes remained at W195, he said these too were set to firm.

In the Black Sea/Med 30,000 tonne gas oil cargoes were fixed at a firm W195. "Vessels are not available before the 25th. Rates are very firm with a lot of cargoes and no ships," an Italian broker said.
The Caribs market was bearish, falling 20 to 30 points to W270 for a 30,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast fixture, Gibson reported.
"Certainly this market will benefit by the number of owners who are turning their attention to Europe and ballasting across the Atlantic," they added. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
